title: Build-a-Knight (Placeholder Wizard Example)
description: An original example of the placeholder-wizard pattern: one long fill-in-the-blank opening builds the player's character and situation entirely from ${prompts}. The prompt IS the experience. Zero story cards.
prompt:
You are ${What is your knight's name?}, ${a title or epithet, e.g. "the Unproven" or "of the Ash Vale"}. You are ${How old are you?} years old, with ${Describe your appearance in a line or two.}. You swore your oath to ${Who or what do you serve? A lord, a faith, a dead friend, only yourself?}.

Your weapon is ${What do you fight with, and is there a story to it?}, and your armor is ${Describe your armor.}. The one thing you carry that you would never sell is ${What is your most prized possession?}.

You are known for one virtue and one flaw: you are ${Name a virtue.}, but also ${Name a flaw.}.

The war ended a year ago and left you with nothing to do and debts to pay. Tonight you are ${Where are you, and what trouble has just found you? Example: in a flooded tavern on the road south, when three of the lord's tax-men kick in the door looking for you by name.}
plotEssentials: You are a knight at loose ends a year after a war that left you with debts and no master.
authorsNote:
Perspective: second person, present tense.
Grounded low fantasy; coin is scarce and reputation matters.
